name: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Principality and Kingdom of Romania to 1918)
native: Principatele Unite ale Moldovei și Țării Românești
wikipedia: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia

predecessors.name: Principality of Wallachia
predecessors.text: Wallachia, one of the two principalities Cuza was elected to rule on 5 February 1859

predecessors.name: Principality of Moldavia
predecessors.text: Moldavia, the other principality (elected prince on 5 January and 5 February 1859 for both)

successors.name: Kingdom of Romania (Greater Romania)
successors.text: Greater Romania: the Old Kingdom plus Bessarabia (1918), Bukovina (28 November 1918) and Transylvania (1 December 1918)

ledger.x: 5 February 1859 (24 January O.S.): Alexandru Ioan Cuza is elected prince of both Moldavia and Wallachia, creating the personal union.
February 1859: Wallachia joins the union with Moldavia under Cuza; the Wallachia dossier ends with the same event.
February 1859: Moldavia joins the union with Wallachia under Cuza.
5 February 1859: the union keeps the Ottoman suzerainty.
3 February 1862 (22 January O.S.): the two principalities formally unite as the Romanian United Principalities and 'Bucharest becomes the sole capital, having shared the role with Iasi from 1859'.

13 July 1866: the first constitution takes effect and gives the state the name 'Romania'; Carol of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen had entered Bucharest on 22 May 1866 after Cuza's forced abdication in February 1866.
21 May 1877 (9 May O.S.): Romania proclaims full independence from the Ottoman suzerain; 'The Ottoman Empire later recognized this in the Treaty of San Stefano' and the powers at Berlin in 1878.
21 May 1877 (9 May O.S.): 'Romania proclaimed itself fully independent' and the infobox closes the vassalage in 1877.
13 July 1878: Southern Bessarabia goes back to Russia.
13 July 1878: Romania receives Dobruja.
March 1881: Romania becomes a kingdom.
June 1913: Romania enters the Second Balkan War.
10 August 1913: the Treaty of Bucharest ends the war ('concluded on 10 August 1913').
10 August 1913: Romania gains Southern Dobruja.
28 August 1916: Romania invades Transylvania.

1 September 1916: Mackensen's army 'attacked north from Bulgaria, starting on 1 September'; 'Bulgarian troops (aided by the German-Bulgarian Detachment) surrounded and stormed the fortress of Turtucaia' and 'The Romanian garrison surrendered on 6 September'; Constanta was 'occupied by the Central Powers on 22 October'.
25 October 1916: the Romanian army is back at its start line.
21 November 1916: 'the German cavalry entered Craiova'.

6 December 1916: 'Bucharest was captured on 6 December by Falkenhayn's cavalry'; by the end of the year 'Southern Romania, including Oltenia, Muntenia, Dobruja, and southern Moldavia, was now in the hands of the Central Powers'; 'The Germans were able to repair the oil fields around Ploiesti'.
December 1916: the government leaves for Iasi.

8 January 1917: 'Mackensen's troops were able to capture Focsani on 8 January', but 'an attempt to break the Siret River line on 19 January failed'; the Romanian line then held in Vrancea (Marasti 24 July 1917, Marasesti to 3 September 1917).
1918: the capital returns from Iasi to Bucharest ('Bucharest (1881-1916, 1918-1947); Iasi (1916-1918)').
9 April 1918 (27 March O.S.): Bessarabia joins Romania.
November 1918: the Bulgarian hold on Dobruja ends with the nullification of the May treaty.
November 1918: the German hold on Oltenia ends.
November 1918: the German hold on Muntenia and Bucharest ends.
November 1918: the German hold on the Focsani area ends.
28 November 1918: Bukovina joins Romania.
1 December 1918: Transylvania joins Romania.
December 1918: the Old Kingdom becomes Greater Romania.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1877-1878) settlement
wars.outcome: Independence recognised and the Dobruja-for-Southern-Bessarabia exchange of the Treaty of Berlin (13 July 1878).

wars.name: Second Balkan War
wars.outcome: Romania acquires Southern Dobruja, 6,960 km2 with Silistra, Tutrakan and Balchik (Treaty of Bucharest, 10 August 1913).

wars.name: Romanian Campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: The Transylvanian advance of 27 August 1916 ends by 25 October; Dobruja falls from 1 September 1916, Bucharest on 6 December 1916; the Siret line holds from January 1917; the Armistice of Focsani (9 December 1917) and the Treaty of Bucharest (7 May 1918…

certainty.note: Treaty frontiers: the Berlin settlement of 1878 (Dobruja and Southern Bessarabia) and the Treaty of Bucharest of 1913 (Southern Dobruja); the Treaty of Paris of 1856 and the Danube line were not opened.
Wartime fronts and occupation; the Bessarabian, Bukovinian and Transylvanian unions of 1918 are declarations, not yet treaty lines.
